scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Your phone holds thousands of photos on a chip smaller than a stamp. Where do they actually live?

scenes.name: cells
scenes.text: Phone storage is flash memory. It's made of billions of tiny cells that can trap electric charge.

scenes.name: bits
scenes.text: Trapped charge, or no charge, stands for a one or a zero. And the charge stays even when the phone is switched off.

scenes.name: levels
scenes.text: Modern chips store several bits in each cell, by trapping different amounts of charge. More levels means more storage in the same space.

scenes.name: photo
scenes.text: A photo is compressed into a few megabytes, millions of ones and zeros, spread across many cells.

scenes.name: controller
scenes.text: Cells slowly wear out with use, so a controller chip spreads your writes evenly across all of them. That's called wear levelling.

scenes.name: space
scenes.text: That's how a one hundred and twenty eight gigabyte phone can fit tens of thousands of photos.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Cells, charge, bits, controller. Memories in a chip. Follow for more on how things really work.
